18: RECOMMENDATION. Suggested speaking time: 75 seconds. Recommend Right-Size & Recover as a staged plan. Keep the existing deck's central scenario and all 20 airports initially. Four trunk markets: Montréal–Toronto, Halifax–Toronto, Halifax–Montréal and Ottawa–Toronto. New markets: London–Toronto, Montréal–Ottawa and Moncton–Halifax. The schedule improvement is $54.57M (28.49 + 19.71 + 6.37), plus $5.2M revenue recovery. Baseline contribution after fiscal-year gates is -$58.40M; result is +$1.37M. Range -$16.88M to +$5.71M combines recapture and revenue-lever scenarios; it is not a statistical confidence interval or a dated forecast. Target FY27–28 matches the executive summary. Central trunk recapture is 100%; the new-market central assumption is 50% recapture of revenue allocated to removed flights. Revenue is not directly matched to individual flights, so retained revenue must be verified in the pilot. All four cost categories on removed flights are assumed avoidable. These are model assumptions, not guaranteed savings. Contribution excludes aircraft ownership, overhead and taxes. No additional savings are added for long-term governance or gates. New-market halving still leaves about $3.9M annual loss centrally, about $2.6M even at full recapture. The proposed six-month trial therefore requires an explicit loss cap and a decision at its end; a 0.8 coverage trigger would already fail initially. The continuation or exit decision is conditional and is not included as extra gain in the headline. Employee effects are material with 27% fewer flights. Prioritize consultation, redeployment and retraining, without promising zero job losses. Voluntary rebooking must preserve the case's refund promise. Sources: analysis/tables/alternatives_matrix.csv; analysis/alternatives.py; analysis/teammate_crosscheck.md; case package pp.6,9,10,17.
19: IMPLEMENTATION. Suggested speaking time: 45 seconds. This is a proposed roadmap from plan approval, not completed actions. Phase 1: Finance validates costs that can actually be removed, including contracts and transition costs. Network Planning establishes route baselines using ticket-to-departure linkage, capacity, demand and connection information absent from the current files. Operations confirms staffing and service constraints. Phase 2: pilot a trunk reduction for an initial 90-day review, monitor weekly and review financial results monthly, then scale only if evidence supports it. Revenue recapture means the share of revenue assigned to cancelled rotations retained on remaining services, adjusted for normal seasonal demand; it is not directly observable from the supplied transaction dates alone. About 90% trunk recapture is the break-even threshold holding the other central assumptions fixed, not a guarantee or an arbitrary service KPI. Track realized savings against the approved avoidable-cost baseline; if either revenue retention or cost savings misses, pause further cuts and reforecast. Start a separate six-month trial when new-market halving begins; review against a pre-approved cumulative loss cap. If it fails, evaluate further reduction, funded community service or exit. Preserve the current 20-airport headline unless the team explicitly chooses a later exit. Confirm whether Halifax A3 and Ottawa A2 are operationally unnecessary, and contract termination/renewal dates, before releasing them; do not count the same gate savings twice or promise savings before contract changes. Phase 3: require positive incremental contribution for any peak-flight addition and review the whole network monthly. Sources: existing slide 17 and alternatives_matrix.csv; teammate_crosscheck.md. Owners, timing and pilot controls are team proposals.
20: RISKS. Suggested speaking time: 30 seconds. Prioritize revenue recapture and cost avoidability because the +$1.4M central contribution has little buffer. The model removes about $73.6M of recorded flight costs, so each 10% that cannot be avoided lowers the gain by about $7.4M. Revenue recovery initiatives are assumptions and may underperform; do not infer that moving an OTA booking directly removes its weather-driven refund risk. The roughly 90% trunk recapture threshold holds other central assumptions fixed. Lack of seats, passenger-to-flight allocation and full overhead costs limits feasibility claims; obtain these before broad rollout. New-market halving is deliberately a temporary trial, not an assertion that these routes become profitable. The downside range on slide 18 does not capture all cost and execution risks. Customer remedies must remain consistent with the case's full-fare refund promise. Safety and maintenance standards remain mandatory throughout any cost reduction. Likelihood labels are qualitative team judgements, not probabilities inferred from the data. Sources: analysis/alternatives.py; alternatives_matrix.csv; teammate_crosscheck.md; FirstByte case package pp.6,9,10,17.
